(a) In General.—Section 1903(i)(21) of the Social Security Act (42 U.S.C. 1396b(i)(21)) is amended by inserting “section 1927(d)(2)(C) (relating to drugs when used for cosmetic purposes or hair growth), except where medically necessary, and” after “drugs described in”. 
    (b) Effective Date.—The amendment made by subsection (a) shall apply with respect to calendar quarters beginning on or after the date of the enactment of this Act.

fable.w: This section only amends a Medicaid payment-exclusion provision to cover cosmetic and hair-growth drugs and sets an effective date. It might be tempting to treat a Medicaid amendment as implying state coordination, but the text sets out no consultation, comment period, hearing, advisory body, rulemaking, or right to sue involving anyone outside the federal government.
fable.s: Section 1903(i)(21) of the Social Security Act (42 U.S.C. 1396b(i)(21)) is amended by inserting “section 1927(d)(2)(C) (relating to drugs when used for cosmetic purposes or hair growth), except where medically necessary, and” after “drugs described in”.

qwen_block.w: This section amends the Social Security Act to exclude certain drugs from Medicaid reimbursement. It defines eligibility criteria for benefits but does not establish any process for public comment, consultation with outside entities, or advisory boards. The interaction described is purely legislative amendment of statutory text regarding benefit coverage.
qwen_block.s: Section 1903(i)(21) of the Social Security Act (42 U.S.C. 1396b(i)(21)) is amended by inserting “section 1927(d)(2)(C) (relating to drugs when used for cosmetic purposes or hair growth), except where medically necessary, and” after “drugs described in”.

opus.w: The section changes Medicaid payment limits for cosmetic and hair-growth drugs and sets the date the change takes effect. It does not require or authorize rulemaking, comment periods, hearings, advisory bodies, consultation with outside parties, or lawsuits. Changing what Medicaid will pay for is not participation.
opus.b: The tempting-but-wrong reading is that amending the Social Security Act's Medicaid payment rules must involve some agency process. It doesn't. The section only adds a category of drugs (cosmetic or hair-growth drugs, unless medically necessary) to a payment prohibition and sets an effective date. Nobody outside the federal government is consulted, and there's no rulemaking, hearing, advisory body or right to sue.

qwen_chat.w: This section amends the Social Security Act to exclude certain drugs from coverage. It does not require or recommend any consultation, public comment, or coordination with outside parties before making this legislative change. The text is purely definitional and procedural regarding the amendment itself, containing no mechanisms for outside participation.
qwen_chat.s: Section 1903(i)(21) of the Social Security Act (42 U.S.C. 1396b(i)(21)) is amended by inserting “section 1927(d)(2)(C) (relating to drugs when used for cosmetic purposes or hair growth), except where medically necessary, and” after “drugs described in”.
qwen_chat.b: Tempting-but-wrong reading: One might argue that amending the Social Security Act to exclude certain drugs from coverage involves a decision that affects the public, and thus implies participation. However, the text itself is purely legislative amendment language; it does not establish any process for public comment, consultation, or advisory input. It simply changes the statutory definition of covered benefits.
